idiom_name: module of functions over arrays of row objects (knex query builder per table)
implementation_notes: JavaScript never needed the class: a Table Module is a module of exported functions (or an object literal) that take a query builder or connection and return arrays of plain row objects - the array is the record set, and the rows are already plain data, so nothing has to be hydrated. knex('orders') is the per-table handle and its builder resolves to an array of objects, which is why the whole classic structure reduces to functions plus a builder. Keep the set-oriented part in SQL (update/delete over a where clause) and use JS iteration only for rules the query cannot express.
pitfalls: knex builders are thenable: forgetting await returns the builder instead of the rows, and the mistake surfaces later as a TypeError on .map or .length.

Money and timestamps arrive as numbers, strings or Date depending on the driver - sum money as integer cents and normalise dates in one place, or the module's totals drift; row objects are also shared by reference, so callers can mutate a record set other code still holds.
